title.zh: 卷503 列傳二百九十 艺術二
title.raw: 卷503 列傳二百九十 艺術二

sentences.zh: 王澍蔣衡徐用錫王文治梁巘梁同書

translations.literal: Wang Shu, Jiang Heng, Xu Yongxi, Wang Wenzhi, Liang Yan, and Liang Tongshu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, Jiang Heng, Xu Yongxi, Wang Wenzhi, Liang Yan, and Liang Tongshu.

sentences.zh: 鄧石如錢伯坰吳育楊沂孫吳熙載梅植之楊亮

translations.literal: Deng Shiru, Qian Boxun, Wu Yu, Yang Yisun, Wu Xizai, Mei Zhizhi, and Yang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shiru, Qian Boxun, Wu Yu, Yang Yisun, Wu Xizai, Mei Zhizhi, and Yang Liang.

sentences.zh: 王澍，字若林，號虛舟，江南金壇人。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, styled Ruolin, with the sobriquet Empty Boat, was a native of Jintan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, whose style was Ruolin and whose sobriquet was Empty Boat, came from Jintan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 績學工文，尤以書名。

translations.literal: He was deeply learned and skilled in literary composition, but was especially renowned for his calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar of wide learning and accomplished prose, he was above all famed for his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，入翰林，累遷戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was successively promoted to supervising secretary in the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign, joined the Hanlin Academy, and rose step by step to supervising secretary in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，詔以六科隸都察院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng reign, an edict ordered that the Six Sections be placed under the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign, an edict placed the Six Sections under the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 澍謂科臣掌封駁，品卑任重，儻隸台臣，將廢科參，偕同官崔致遠、康五端抗疏力爭。

translations.literal: Shu argued that section officials were charged with sealing and rejecting memorials; though low in rank their responsibility was weighty—if they were subordinated to censorate officials, section memorials would be abolished. Together with his colleagues Cui Zhiyuan and Kang Wuduan he submitted a forceful memorial in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Shu held that section officials handled the sealing and rejection of memorials: humble in rank yet heavy in duty. If they were made subordinate to censorate officers, section memorials would cease. He joined colleagues Cui Zhiyuan and Kang Wuduan in a strenuous memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 立召詰之，從容奏對，上意稍解，遂改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned for interrogation; Shu answered composedly, the emperor's anger eased somewhat, and he was transferred to be a vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned at once for questioning, Shu replied with composure; the emperor's temper softened a little, and he was reassigned as a vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 越二年，告歸，益耽書，名播海內。

translations.literal: Two years later he requested leave to retire, devoted himself ever more to calligraphy, and his fame spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on he retired home, threw himself ever deeper into calligraphy, and his name rang across the land.

sentences.zh: 摹古名搨殆遍，四體並工。

translations.literal: He copied nearly every famous ancient rubbing; he was accomplished in all four script types.
translations.idiomatic: He traced nearly every celebrated ancient rubbing and mastered all four script forms.

sentences.zh: 於唐賢歐、褚兩家，致力尤深​​，輒跋尾自道所得。

translations.literal: Of the Two Tang masters Ouyang and Chu he devoted himself especially deeply, and would invariably add a colophon at the end describing what he had gained.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself above all to the Tang masters Ouyang Xun and Chu Suiliang, and habitually appended colophons explaining what he had learned.

sentences.zh: 後內閣學士翁方綱持論與異，謂其篆書得古法，行書次之，正書又次之。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Secretary Weng Fanggang held a different view, saying his seal script attained the ancient method, running script came next, and regular script after that.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Secretary Weng Fanggang disagreed, ranking his seal script as true to ancient methods, his running script next, and his regular script last.

sentences.zh: 所著題跋及淳化閣帖考正，並行於世。

translations.literal: His colophons and his Critical Examination of the Chunhua Pavilion Rubbings were both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His colophons and his Critical Examination of the Chunhua Pavilion Rubbings both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 自明、清之際，工書者，河北以王鐸、傅山為冠，繼則江左王鴻緒、姜宸英、何焯、汪士鋐、張照等，接踵而起，多見他傳。

translations.literal: From the Ming–Qing transition onward, among masters of calligraphy Hebei took Wang Duo and Fu Shan as foremost; then in the lower Yangtze region Wang Hongxu, Jiang Chenying, He Chao, Wang Shihong, Zhang Zhao, and others rose in succession—most appear in other biographies.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ming–Qing transition on, the leading calligraphers of Hebei were Wang Duo and Fu Shan; in the lower Yangtze, Wang Hongxu, Jiang Chenying, He Chao, Wang Shihong, Zhang Zhao, and others followed one after another—most are treated in other chapters.

sentences.zh: 大抵淵源出於明文徵明、董其昌兩家，鴻緒、照為董氏嫡派，焯及澍則於文氏為近。

translations.literal: For the most part their lineage derived from the Ming masters Wen Zhengming and Dong Qichang; Hongxu and Zhao were direct heirs of the Dong school, while He Chao and Shu stood closer to the Wen line.
translations.idiomatic: Their lineages traced mainly to the Ming masters Wen Zhengming and Dong Qichang: Hongxu and Zhao were orthodox followers of Dong, while He Chao and Shu leaned toward Wen.

sentences.zh: 澍論書尤詳，一時所宗。

translations.literal: Shu's treatises on calligraphy were especially detailed, and he was the authority of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's writings on calligraphy were the most detailed of the day, and his age looked to him as its authority.

sentences.zh: 蔣衡，改名振生，字湘帆，晚號拙老人。

translations.literal: Jiang Heng changed his name to Zhensheng, styled Xiangfan, and in later years took the sobriquet Clumsy Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Heng, who changed his name to Zhensheng, styled himself Xiangfan and in old age called himself the Clumsy Old Man.

sentences.zh: 與澍同里。

translations.literal: He was from the same district as Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fellow townsman of Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 鍵戶十二年，寫十三經。

translations.literal: He shut his door for twelve years and wrote out the Thirteen Classics.
translations.idiomatic: For twelve years he shut himself indoors and copied out the entire Thirteen Classics in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，進上，高宗命刻石國學，授衡國子監學正，終不出。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign he presented his work to the throne; the Gaozong Emperor ordered it carved in stone at the Imperial Academy and appointed Heng director of studies at the Directorate of Education, but he never took office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he presented his work to the court; the emperor ordered it cut in stone at the Imperial Academy and named Heng director of studies at the Directorate of Education, yet he never emerged from retirement.

sentences.zh: 衡早歲好遊，足跡半海內，觀碑關中，獲晉、唐以來名跡，臨摹三百餘種，曰拙存堂臨古帖。

translations.literal: In his early years Heng loved travel; his footsteps reached half the realm. Viewing steles in Guanzhong he obtained famous works from Jin and Tang onward, copied more than three hundred kinds, and titled the collection Rubbings of Ancient Models from the Clumsy Preservation Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Heng loved to travel and ranged over half the empire. In Guanzhong he studied steles, gathered celebrated works from Jin and Tang times onward, and traced more than three hundred pieces, which he collected as Rubbings of Ancient Models from the Clumsy Preservation Hall.

sentences.zh: 晚與澍相期斫勝，每臨一書，相從質證。

translations.literal: In later years he and Shu arranged contests of skill; whenever either copied a work they would go together to verify and discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he and Shu held friendly contests: whenever one copied a piece, the other came along to judge and debate it.

sentences.zh: 子驥，孫和，並以書世其家。

translations.literal: His son Ji and grandson He both carried on the family's fame through calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji and grandson He both upheld the family name through calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 驥尤精分隸，著漢隸譌體集、古帖字體、續書法論各一卷，兼工畫。

translations.literal: Ji was especially skilled in clerical and demotic scripts, authored one fascicle each of Collected Errata in Han Clerical Forms, Character Forms in Ancient Rubbings, and Continuation of Treatises on Calligraphy, and was also accomplished in painting.
translations.idiomatic: Ji excelled above all in clerical and demotic script, wrote one fascicle each on Han clerical forms, ancient rubbing letterforms, and calligraphic theory, and painted as well.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「漢、魏字體不同，性情各異。

translations.literal: He said: "The letterforms of Han and Wei differ, and their temperaments are each distinct.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Han and Wei scripts differ in form, and each bears its own character.

sentences.zh: 書須懸臂中鋒，而用力以和平為主。

translations.literal: In writing one must suspend the arm and use the central tip of the brush, and in applying force take evenness and harmony as the main principle.
translations.idiomatic: Writing requires the suspended arm and centered brush-tip; strength should above all seek balance and ease.

sentences.zh: 作畫之提頓逆折，參差映帶，其理一爾。

translations.literal: The lifting, pressing, reversing, and folding in painting, with their staggered echoes and linkages—the principle is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The lift, press, turn, and fold of brushwork in painting, with its staggered echoes—the principle is one and the same.

sentences.zh: 」皆闡明其先說。

translations.literal: "—all of which elaborated his forebears' doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: "—each line elaborating the teachings of his forebears.

sentences.zh: 徐用錫，字壇長，宿遷人，佔籍大興。

translations.literal: Xu Yongxi, styled Tanchang, was a native of Suqian with household registration at Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yongxi, styled Tanchang, came from Suqian but was registered at Daxing.

sentences.zh: 登鄉舉，康熙四十八年進士，官翰林院編修。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination, became a metropolitan graduate in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, and served as compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After winning the provincial degree he took the metropolitan examination in Kangxi 48 and served as a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 從李光地遊，究心樂律、音韻、歷數、書法。

translations.literal: He studied under Li Guangdi and devoted himself to music theory, phonology, calendrical science, and calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: A disciple of Li Guangdi, he pursued music theory, phonology, calendrical science, and calligraphy with equal seriousness.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，分校會試，嚴絕請託，銜之者反嗾言官劾其把持闈事，聖祖原之，終以浮議罷歸。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination and sternly refused all solicitations; those who resented him in turn incited censors to impeach him for controlling examination affairs. The Sacred Ancestor pardoned him, but he was ultimately dismissed and sent home on account of loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: In year 54 he helped grade the metropolitan examination and refused every favor outright. Enemies set censors on him, charging that he controlled the examination hall. Kangxi forgave him, yet he was still sent home amid the gossip.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，起授翰林院侍讀，年已八十。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign he was recalled and appointed reader in the Hanlin Academy, already eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he was recalled as Hanlin reader—by then he was eighty.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he requested leave to retire and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired again and died at home.

sentences.zh: 用錫鄉舉出姜宸英之門，與何焯同為光地客，論書多與二家相出入。

translations.literal: Yongxi's provincial degree came through Jiang Chenying's school; he and He Chao were both clients of Li Guangdi, and his views on calligraphy largely agreed or disagreed with those two houses.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi had studied under Jiang Chenying before the provincial exam; he and He Chao were both protégés of Li Guangdi, and his calligraphic opinions largely tracked or diverged from those two circles.

sentences.zh: 精於鑑別古人，言筆法亦多心得，著字學劄記二卷，載圭美堂集中。

translations.literal: He was expert in authenticating ancient works; his remarks on brush technique also contained many insights of his own. He authored two fascicles of Notes on Letter Studies, preserved in the Guimei Hall collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: A keen judge of antiquities, he had much to say on brush technique from personal insight. His two fascicles of Notes on Letter Studies appear in the Guimei Hall collection.

sentences.zh: 王文治，字禹卿，江蘇丹徒人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenzhi, styled Yuqing, was a native of Dantu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenzhi, styled Yuqing, came from Dantu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 生有夙慧，十二歲能詩，即工書。

translations.literal: He was born with innate brilliance; at twelve he could compose poetry and was already skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted from birth, he was writing poetry at twelve and already accomplished at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 長游京師，從翰林院侍讀全魁使琉球，文字播於海外。

translations.literal: When grown he traveled to the capital; he accompanied Hanlin reader Quan Kui on a mission to Ryukyu, and his writing spread overseas.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he went to the capital and accompanied Hanlin reader Quan Kui on the Ryukyu mission; his writing soon spread beyond China.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十五年，成一甲三名進士，授翰林院編修。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he placed third among the first-rank metropolitan graduates and was appointed compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 35 he finished third in the first rank of the metropolitan examination and became a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，大考第一，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: After three years he ranked first in the grand examination and was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he topped the palace examination and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 出為雲南臨安知府，因事鐫級，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan; because of an affair his rank was reduced by inscription, and he begged leave on grounds of illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan, he lost rank after a scandal and retired home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 後當復官，厭吏事，遂不出，往來吳、越間，主講杭州、鎮江書院。

translations.literal: Later, when he was due to be restored to office, he wearied of administrative affairs and would not emerge, traveling between Wu and Yue and serving as lecturer at academies in Hangzhou and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When reinstatement came due he had had enough of official life and stayed away, moving between Jiangsu and Zhejiang as lecturer at academies in Hangzhou and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 高宗南巡，至錢塘僧寺，見文治書碑，大賞愛之。

translations.literal: On the Gaozong Emperor's southern tour, when he reached a Buddhist temple in Qiantang and saw a stele inscribed by Wenzhi, he greatly admired it.
translations.idiomatic: On his southern tour the emperor stopped at a Qiantang monastery, saw a stele Wenzhi had inscribed, and admired it deeply.

sentences.zh: 內廷有以告，招之出者，亦不應。

translations.literal: Someone in the inner court reported this; when he was summoned to come forth, he still would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the inner court and he was summoned—but he would not come.

sentences.zh: 喜聲伎，行輒以歌伶一部自隨，辨論音律，窮極幽渺。

translations.literal: He delighted in music and entertainers; whenever he traveled he took a whole troupe of singers with him, debating musical theory to the utmost subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music and song; on the road he traveled with a full company of singers and debated pitch and rhythm down to the finest shade.

sentences.zh: 客至張樂，窮朝暮不倦。

translations.literal: When guests arrived he would set out music and carry on from morning to night without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: When guests came he staged music from dawn to dusk without flagging.

sentences.zh: 海內求書者，多有餽遺，率費於聲伎。

translations.literal: Those throughout the realm who sought his writing often sent gifts, which he generally spent on music and entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: Patrons across the land paid handsomely for his writing—and he spent it almost entirely on music and song.

sentences.zh: 然客散，默然禪定，夜坐，肋未嘗至席。

translations.literal: Yet when guests had departed he would sit in silent meditation; in night sitting his ribs never touched the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once guests had gone he sat in silent meditation through the night, his ribs never touching the mat.

sentences.zh: 持佛戒，自言吾詩與書皆禪理也。

translations.literal: He kept Buddhist precepts and said of himself, "My poetry and calligraphy are both Chan principle."
translations.idiomatic: He kept the Buddhist precepts and said, "My poetry and my calligraphy are both Chan."

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 所著詩集外有快雨堂題跋，略見論書之旨。

translations.literal: Besides his collected poems he left Kuaiyu Hall Colophons, which give a glimpse of his views on calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Besides his poetry he left Kuaiyu Hall Colophons, which sketch his calligraphic ideals.

sentences.zh: 文治書名並時與劉墉相埒，人稱之曰「濃墨宰相，淡墨探花」。

translations.literal: Wenzhi's fame in calligraphy at the time matched Liu Yong's; people called them "the Chancellor of Thick Ink and the Flower of Pale Ink."
translations.idiomatic: In his day Wenzhi's calligraphic fame rivaled Liu Yong's; people dubbed them "the Chancellor of Thick Ink" and "the Flower of Pale Ink."

sentences.zh: 與姚鼐交最深，論最契，當時書名，鼐不及文治之遠播；

translations.literal: He was closest in friendship and most in accord in discussion with Yao Nai; at that time Yao's fame in calligraphy did not spread as far as Wenzhi's;
translations.idiomatic: His closest friend and keenest interlocutor was Yao Nai; at the time Yao's calligraphic fame did not travel as far as Wenzhi's;

sentences.zh: 後包世臣極推鼐書，與劉墉並列上品，名轉出文治上。

translations.literal: later Bao Shichen greatly praised Yao's writing, placing it with Liu Yong in the highest rank, and Yao's name in turn rose above Wenzhi's.
translations.idiomatic: later Bao Shichen ranked Yao's writing with Liu Yong among the finest, and Yao's reputation eclipsed Wenzhi's.

sentences.zh: 梁巘，字聞山，安徽亳州人。

translations.literal: Liang Yan, styled Wenshan, was a native of Bozhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yan, styled Wenshan, came from Bozhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十七年舉人，官四川巴縣知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate and served as magistrate of Baxian in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He took the provincial degree in Qianlong 27 and served as magistrate of Baxian in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 晚辭官，主講壽春書院，以工李北海書名於世。

translations.literal: In later years he resigned office and lectured at the Shouchun Academy, becoming renowned in the world for his mastery of Li Beihai's style.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned late in life to lecture at the Shouchun Academy and won fame for mastering the manner of Li Yong of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 初為咸安宮教習，至京師，聞欽天監正何國宗曾以事系刑部，時尚書張照亦以他事在系，得其筆法，因詣家就問。

translations.literal: At first he was an instructor at the Xian'an Palace; when he reached the capital he heard that Director of the Astronomical Bureau He Guozong had once been detained in the Ministry of Justice over an affair, and that at the time Minister Zhang Zhao was also imprisoned on another matter—he had obtained their brush methods and therefore went to their homes to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an instructor at the Xian'an Palace. In the capital he learned that Astronomical Bureau director He Guozong and Minister Zhang Zhao had both once been held in the Ministry of Justice—and had there revealed their brush methods. Yan went to their homes to learn from them.

sentences.zh: 國宗年已八十餘，病不能對客，遣一孫傳語。

translations.literal: Guozong was already over eighty, ill and unable to receive guests, and sent a grandson to convey his words.
translations.idiomatic: Guozong was past eighty, too ill to receive visitors, and sent a grandson to speak for him.

sentences.zh: 巘質以所聞，國宗答曰：「君已得之矣。

translations.literal: Yan questioned him about what he had heard; Guozong replied: "You have already obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked about what he had learned. Guozong answered: "You already have it.

sentences.zh: 」贈以所臨米、黃二帖。

translations.literal: " He presented him with his copies of the two rubbings by Mi and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him his traced copies of works by Mi Fu and Huang Tingjian.

sentences.zh: 後巘以語金壇段玉裁曰：「執筆之法，指以運臂，臂以運身。

translations.literal: Later Yan told Duan Yucai of Jintan: "The method of holding the brush: the fingers move the arm, the arm moves the body.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan told Duan Yucai of Jintan: "In holding the brush, the fingers move the arm, and the arm moves the whole body.

sentences.zh: 凡捉筆，以大指尖與食指尖相對，筆正直在兩指尖之間，兩指尖相接如環，兩指本以上平，可安酒杯。

translations.literal: Whenever one grasps the brush, the tips of the thumb and forefinger face each other, the brush standing straight between the two finger-tips; the two tips meet like a ring, and from the knuckles upward they are level so that a wine cup could be set there.
translations.idiomatic: To grasp the brush, set the thumb-tip and forefinger-tip opposite each other with the brush upright between them. The tips should meet like a ring, level from the knuckles up—steady enough to balance a wine cup.

sentences.zh: 平其肘，腕不附幾，肘圓而兩指與筆正當胸，令全身之力，行於臂而湊於兩指尖。

translations.literal: Level the elbow; the wrist does not rest on the table. The elbow is rounded and the two fingers with the brush are directly before the chest, so that the strength of the whole body passes through the arm and gathers at the two finger-tips.
translations.idiomatic: Level the elbow and keep the wrist off the desk. With the elbow rounded and brush before the chest, let the body's full force run through the arm and collect at the fingertips.

sentences.zh: 兩指尖不圓如環，或如環而不平，則捉之也不緊，臂之力尚不能出，而況於身？

translations.literal: If the two finger-tips do not form a ring, or form a ring but are not level, then the grasp is not tight—the arm's force cannot yet emerge, how much less the body's?
translations.idiomatic: If the fingertips do not form a true ring, or form one but are not level, the grip is loose—the arm's force cannot emerge, let alone the body's.

sentences.zh: 緊則身之力全湊於指尖，而何有於臂？

translations.literal: When tight, the body's force entirely gathers at the finger-tips—what need is there for the arm?
translations.idiomatic: When the grip is tight, the body's force gathers wholly at the fingertips—what role remains for the arm alone?

sentences.zh: 古人知指之不能運臂也，故使指頂相接以固筆，筆管可斷，指鍥痛不可勝，而後字中有力。

translations.literal: The ancients knew that the fingers alone cannot move the arm, and therefore made the finger-tops meet to secure the brush—the shaft might break, but the fingers' wedged pain would be unbearable, and only then would strength enter the characters.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients knew fingers alone cannot drive the arm, so they joined the finger-tops to lock the brush: the shaft might snap before the wedged fingers relented—only then did strength enter the stroke.

sentences.zh: 其以大指與食指也，謂之單勾；

translations.literal: Using the thumb and forefinger is called the single hook;
translations.idiomatic: Holding with thumb and forefinger alone is called the single hook;

sentences.zh: 其以大指與食指中指也，謂之雙勾；

translations.literal: using the thumb with forefinger and middle finger is called the double hook;
translations.idiomatic: using thumb, forefinger, and middle finger is the double hook;

sentences.zh: 中指者，所以輔食指之力也，總謂之'撥鐙法'。

translations.literal: the middle finger assists the forefinger's force—all together called the "stirrup-pressing method."
translations.idiomatic: the middle finger assists the forefinger—all of this is the stirrup-pressing method.

sentences.zh: 王獻之七、八歲時學書，右軍從旁掣其筆不得，即謂此法。

translations.literal: When Wang Xianzhi was seven or eight and learning to write, the Right General tried to pull the brush from beside him and could not—this is that method.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xianzhi was seven or eight, Wang Xizhi could not pull the brush from his hand—that is this method.

sentences.zh: 捨此法，皆旁門外道。

translations.literal: Apart from this method, all are side gates and heterodox paths.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon this method and you are on a side path.

sentences.zh: 二王以後，至唐、宋、元、明諸大家，口口相傳如是，董宗伯以授王司農鴻緒，司農以授張文敏，吾聞而知之。

translations.literal: After the Two Wangs down through the great masters of Tang, Song, Yuan, and Ming it was passed mouth to mouth thus; Master Dong gave it to Minister of Agriculture Wang Hongxu, Hongxu gave it to Zhang Wenmin, and I heard and learned it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Two Wangs through Tang, Song, Yuan, and Ming masters it passed mouth to mouth; Dong Qichang taught Wang Hongxu, Hongxu taught Zhang Zhao, and I heard it from them.

sentences.zh: 本朝但有一張文敏耳，他未為善。

translations.literal: In our dynasty there is only one Zhang Wenmin; the rest have not done well.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty only Zhang Zhao truly mastered it; the rest fell short.

sentences.zh: 王虛舟用筆祗得一半，蔣湘帆知握筆而少作字樂趣。

translations.literal: Wang Empty Boat has attained only half in brush use; Jiang Xiangfan knows how to hold the brush but lacks the joy of writing characters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu grasped only half the method; Jiang Heng knew how to hold the brush but lacked the joy of writing.

sentences.zh: 世人但言無火氣，不知火氣使盡，而後可言無火氣也。

translations.literal: People only speak of having no fiery vigor, not knowing that only after fiery vigor is fully spent can one speak of having none.
translations.idiomatic: People praise "lack of fire" without knowing that only after fire is fully spent can one speak of its absence.

sentences.zh: 如此捉筆，則筆心不偏，中心透紙，紙上颯颯有聲。

translations.literal: Holding the brush thus, the brush-heart does not deviate; the center penetrates the paper, and on the paper there is a rustling sound.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the brush this way and the core stays true, the center pierces the paper, and the sheet rustles under the stroke.

sentences.zh: 直畫粗者濃墨兩分，中如有絲界，筆心為之主也。

translations.literal: In thick vertical strokes of heavy ink there are two parts, with a silk-like boundary in the middle—the brush-heart is master of it.
translations.idiomatic: A thick vertical in heavy ink splits in two with a filament down the center—the brush-heart rules the stroke.

sentences.zh: 如此捉筆，則必堅紙作字，輭薄紙當之易破。

translations.literal: Holding the brush thus one must write on firm paper; soft thin paper will easily tear under it.
translations.idiomatic: With this grip you must write on stiff paper—thin soft sheets tear at once.

sentences.zh: 其橫、直、撇、捺皆與今人殊，筆鋒所指，方向迥異，筆心總在每筆之中，無少偏也。

translations.literal: Their horizontal, vertical, left-falling, and right-falling strokes all differ from those of today; the direction the brush-tip points is utterly different, and the brush-heart is always in the center of each stroke without the slightest deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Their horizontals, verticals, and falling strokes differ from modern practice; the tip points another way, yet the brush-heart stays centered in every stroke.

sentences.zh: 古人所謂屋漏痕、折釵股、錐畫沙、印印泥者，於此可悟入。

translations.literal: What the ancients called "leaks in the roof," "broken hairpin legs," "awl drawing on sand," and "seal pressing into mud"—through this one may enter into understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients' "roof-leak trace," "broken hairpin," "awl on sand," and "seal in clay"—here one may grasp them.

sentences.zh: 」巘少著述，所傳緒論僅此。

translations.literal: " Yan wrote little; the transmitted threads of his theory are only this much.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan wrote little; this is all that survives of his teaching.

sentences.zh: 當時與梁同書並稱，巘曰「北梁」，同書曰「南梁」。

translations.literal: At the time he and Liang Tongshu were spoken of together; Yan was called "Northern Liang" and Tongshu "Southern Liang."
translations.idiomatic: He and Liang Tongshu were paired in fame as "Northern Liang" and "Southern Liang."

sentences.zh: 梁同書，字元穎，晚號山舟，浙江錢塘人，大學士詩正子。

translations.literal: Liang Tongshu, styled Yuanying, with the late sobriquet Mountain Boat, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang and son of Grand Secretary Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tongshu, styled Yuanying and in old age called Mountain Boat, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang and was the son of Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，會試未第，高宗特賜與殿試，入翰林，大考，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he failed the metropolitan examination, but the Gaozong Emperor specially granted him participation in the palace examination; he entered the Hanlin, and in the grand examination was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 he failed the metropolitan exam, but the emperor admitted him to the palace examination anyway. He entered the Hanlin and, after the grand examination, became expositor.

sentences.zh: 淡於榮利，未老，因疾不出。

translations.literal: Indifferent to glory and profit, before he was old he ceased to emerge on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Indifferent to rank and gain, he withdrew while still young, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 晚年重宴鹿鳴，加侍講學士銜。

translations.literal: In his later years he was again feasted at the Deer Call banquet and given the additional title of expositor academician.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he was again honored at the Deer Call feast and given the title of expositor academician.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 好書出天性，十二歲能為擘窠大字。

translations.literal: His love of calligraphy came from innate nature; at twelve he could write large characters in split-stroke style.
translations.idiomatic: He loved writing by nature and at twelve could execute large display characters.

sentences.zh: 初法顏、柳，中年用米法，七十後乃變化。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yan and Liu; in mid-life he used Mi's method; only after seventy did he transform.
translations.idiomatic: He began with Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan, turned to Mi Fu in midlife, and found his own voice only after seventy.

sentences.zh: 名滿天下，求書者紙日數束，日本、琉球皆重之。

translations.literal: His fame filled the realm; those who sought his writing brought several bundles of paper daily; Japan and Ryukyu all prized him.
translations.idiomatic: His fame filled the world; patrons arrived daily with bundles of paper, and Japan and Ryukyu prized his work.

sentences.zh: 嘗與張燕昌論書，略曰：「古人云『筆力直透紙背』，當與天馬行空參看。

translations.literal: He once discussed calligraphy with Zhang Yanchang, saying in summary: "The ancients said 'brush force penetrates straight through the paper's back'—this should be read together with 'the heavenly horse ranges through empty space.'
translations.idiomatic: Discussing calligraphy with Zhang Yanchang, he said in part: "When the ancients speak of brush force piercing the back of the paper, read it alongside 'the heavenly horse ranges through empty space.'"

sentences.zh: 今人誤認透紙，便如藥山所云『看穿牛皮』，終無是處。

translations.literal: People today mistakenly take penetrating the paper to mean, as Yaoshan said, 'seeing through ox-hide'—there is ultimately no point in it.
translations.idiomatic: Modern readers mistake penetration for Yaoshan's 'seeing through ox-hide'—a dead end.

sentences.zh: 蓋透紙者，狀其精氣結撰墨光浮溢耳，彼用筆如游絲者，何嘗不透紙背耶？

translations.literal: For penetrating the paper describes how vital essence gathers and ink-light overflows; those who use the brush like drifting silk—have they not also penetrated the paper's back?
translations.idiomatic: Penetration describes spirit gathering and ink-light overflowing. Writers who use silk-fine strokes—do they not also pierce the paper's back?

sentences.zh: 用腕力使極輭之筆自見，譬如人持一彊者，使之直，則無所用力；

translations.literal: Using wrist force makes an extremely soft brush reveal itself; it is like a person holding something stiff—if he makes it straight, he need apply no force;
translations.idiomatic: Wrist force reveals the softest brush. Hold something stiff and straighten it—you need no effort;

sentences.zh: 持一弱者，慾不使之偃，則全腕之力，自然集於兩指端。

translations.literal: holding something weak, if he wishes not to let it bend, then the whole wrist's force naturally gathers at the two finger-ends.
translations.idiomatic: hold something weak and keep it from bending—the whole wrist's force gathers at the fingertips.

sentences.zh: 其實書者只知指運，而不知有腕力也。

translations.literal: In truth calligraphers only know finger movement and do not know there is wrist force.
translations.idiomatic: In truth most writers know only finger movement and forget the wrist.

sentences.zh: 藏鋒之說，非筆如鈍錐之謂，自來書家從無不出鋒者，只是處處留得筆住，不使直走。

translations.literal: The doctrine of hiding the tip does not mean a brush like a blunt awl; calligraphers from of old have never failed to bring out the tip—they only everywhere keep the brush dwelling, not letting it run straight.
translations.idiomatic: Hiding the tip does not mean a blunt awl. Masters have always brought the tip out—they simply keep the brush dwelling at every turn instead of letting it run straight.

sentences.zh: 筆耍輭，輭則遒；

translations.literal: The brush must be soft; when soft it becomes forceful;
translations.idiomatic: The brush should be supple—suppleness yields vigor;

sentences.zh: 筆要長，長則靈；

translations.literal: the brush must be long; when long it becomes spirited;
translations.idiomatic: it should be long—length brings life;

sentences.zh: 筆耍飽，飽則腴；

translations.literal: the brush must be full; when full it becomes rich;
translations.idiomatic: it must be well loaded—full ink gives fullness to the stroke;

sentences.zh: 落筆耍快，快則意出。

translations.literal: Putting the brush down must be quick; when quick the idea emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The stroke must fall quickly—speed brings the idea forth.

sentences.zh: 書家燥鋒曰渴筆，畫家亦有枯筆，二字判然不同。

translations.literal: Calligraphers call a dry tip a thirsty brush; painters also have a withered brush—the two terms are clearly different.
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphers speak of a "thirsty" brush for a dry tip; painters speak of a "withered" brush—the two words are utterly distinct.

sentences.zh: 渴則不潤，枯則死矣。

translations.literal: Thirsty then lacks moisture; withered then is dead.
translations.idiomatic: Thirst means lack of moisture; withered means lifeless stroke.

sentences.zh: ​​今人喜用硬筆故枯。

translations.literal: People today delight in using stiff brushes and therefore their work is withered.
translations.idiomatic: Modern writers favor stiff brushes—that is why their strokes look dead.

sentences.zh: 帖教人看，不教人摹。

translations.literal: Rubbings teach people to look, not to trace.
translations.idiomatic: Model books are for study, not for slavish copying.

sentences.zh: 今人只是刻舟求劍，將古人書摹畫如小兒寫仿本，就便形似，豈復有我？

translations.literal: People today only mark the boat to seek the sword, tracing ancient writing like children copying models—if it happens to resemble the form, how can there still be a self?
translations.idiomatic: Today people chase forms like the man who marked the boat to find his sword, copying ancients as children copy models. Surface likeness is not selfhood.

sentences.zh: 字耍有氣，氣須從熟得來。

translations.literal: Characters must have breath; breath must come from mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Writing must have breath, and breath comes only through mastery.

sentences.zh: 有氣則有勢，大小、長短、高下、欹整，隨筆所至，自然貫注，成一片段，卻著不得絲毫擺佈，熟後自知。

translations.literal: With breath there is momentum; large and small, long and short, high and low, leaning and straight—all follow where the brush goes, naturally flowing through and forming one passage, yet not admitting the slightest contrivance; after mastery one knows it oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Breath brings momentum: size, length, height, tilt, and balance follow the brush and fuse into one flowing passage without the least forced arrangement—only practice teaches this.

sentences.zh: 中鋒之法，筆提得起，自然中，亦未嘗無兼用側鋒處，總為我一縷筆尖所使，雖不中亦中。

translations.literal: The method of the centered tip: if the brush can be lifted, it is naturally centered; there are also places where the side tip is used together—altogether they are moved by my single thread of brush-point; though not centered, they are still centered.
translations.idiomatic: In the centered-tip method, a brush that lifts stays centered; side-tip moments exist too, yet one filament of the point governs all—even when off-center, it is center.

sentences.zh: 亂頭粗服非字也，求逸則野，求舊則拙，此處不可有半點名心在。

translations.literal: Disheveled hair and coarse dress are not writing; seeking ease becomes rustic, seeking antiquity becomes clumsy—here one must not have the slightest thought of making a name.
translations.idiomatic: Wild hair and rough dress are not calligraphy; chasing ease turns rustic, chasing antiquity turns clumsy—here ambition for fame must not enter.

sentences.zh: 」同書平生書旨，與梁巘之異同，具見於此。

translations.literal: " Tongshu's lifelong principles of calligraphy, and their agreements and differences with Liang Yan's, are fully seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: " Here one sees Tongshu's lifelong calligraphic ideals and how they agreed and differed from Liang Yan's.

sentences.zh: 鄧石如，初名避仁宗諱，遂以字行，改字頑伯，安徽懷寧人。

translations.literal: Deng Shiru—his original given name avoided the taboo of Emperor Renzong, so he went by his style name, later changing his style to Wanbo—was a native of Huaining in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shiru, whose birth name avoided the Renzong taboo so that he was known by his style (later changed to Wanbo), came from Huaining in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 居皖公山下，又號完白山人。

translations.literal: He dwelt beneath Mount Wan Gong and also styled himself the Mountain Man of Wanbai.
translations.idiomatic: He lived below Mount Wan Gong and also called himself the Hermit of Wanbai.

sentences.zh: 少產僻鄉，鮮聞見，獨好刻石，仿漢人印篆甚工。

translations.literal: Born in a remote village with little exposure, he alone loved carving stone and imitated Han seal script with great skill.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in an isolated hamlet with few models, he devoted himself to stone carving and copied Han seal script with remarkable skill.

sentences.zh: 弱冠孤貧，遊壽州，梁巘見其篆書，驚為筆勢渾鷙，而未盡得古法。

translations.literal: At twenty he was orphaned and poor, traveled to Shouzhou; Liang Yan saw his seal script and was startled by its vigorous, fierce brush momentum, yet judged that he had not fully attained the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor at twenty, he went to Shouzhou. Liang Yan marveled at the bold, fierce energy of his seal script, yet felt he had not fully mastered antique methods.

sentences.zh: 介謁江寧梅鏐，都御史成子也。

translations.literal: He was introduced to Mei Liu of Jiangning, son of the Censor-in-chief Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan introduced him to Mei Liu of Nanjing, son of the censor-in-chief Mei Cheng.

sentences.zh: 家多L3藏金石善本，盡出示之，為具衣食楮墨，使專肄習。

translations.literal: The household possessed many fine bronze and stone rubbings in its collection; all were shown him, and food, clothing, paper, and ink were provided so that he might devote himself wholly to study.
translations.idiomatic: The Mei household owned many fine bronze and stone rubbings and showed him all of them, supplying food, clothing, paper, and ink so he could study full time.

sentences.zh: 好石鼓文，李斯嶧山碑、泰山刻石，漢開母石闕，燉煌太守碑，吳蘇建國山碑，皇像天發神讖碑，唐李陽冰城隍廟碑、三墳記，每種臨摹各百本。

translations.literal: He loved the Stone Drum Inscriptions, Li Si's Mount Yi stele and Mount Tai carving, the Han Kai Mother stone que, the Dunhuang Prefect stele, Wu Su Jian's Guoshan stele, the Huangxiang Heavenly Revelation stele, and Tang Li Yangbing's City God Temple stele and Record of the Three Mounds—of each he made a hundred traced copies.
translations.idiomatic: He traced the Stone Drums, Li Si's Yi Mountain and Mount Tai inscriptions, the Han Kai Mother que, the Dunhuang Prefect stele, Wu Su Jian's Guoshan stele, the Huangxiang revelation stele, and Li Yangbing's City God Temple and Three Mounds records—a hundred copies of each.

sentences.zh: 又苦篆體不備，寫說文解字二十本。

translations.literal: He also grieved that seal forms were incomplete and wrote out twenty copies of the Shuowen Jiezi.
translations.idiomatic: Finding seal forms incomplete, he copied the Shuowen Jiezi twenty times over.

sentences.zh: 帝搜三代鐘鼎，秦、漢瓦當、碑額。

translations.literal: The emperor searched out Three Dynasties bells and tripods, Qin and Han roof-tile ends and stele crowns.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Three Dynasties bronzes and Qin–Han tile ends and stele crowns.

sentences.zh: 五年，篆書成。

translations.literal: In five years his seal script was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: After five years his seal script was complete.

sentences.zh: 乃學漢分，臨史晨前、後碑，華山碑，白石神君，張遷，潘校官，孔羨，受禪，大饗諸碑，各五十本。

translations.literal: Then he studied Han demotic script, copying the front and back Shi Chen steles, the Mount Hua stele, the White Stone Spirit Lord, Zhang Qian, Pan the School Official, Kong Xian, the Accession to the Throne, the Grand Sacrifice, and other steles—fifty copies of each.
translations.idiomatic: He then studied Han clerical script, tracing the Shi Chen front and back steles, Mount Hua, White Stone Spirit Lord, Zhang Qian, Pan the School Official, Kong Xian, Accession to the Throne, Grand Sacrifice, and others—fifty copies apiece.

sentences.zh: 三年，分書成。

translations.literal: In three years his demotic script was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later his clerical script was complete.

sentences.zh: 石如篆法以二李為宗，縱橫闢闔，得之史籀，稍參隸意，殺鋒以取勁折，字體微方，與秦、漢當額為近。

translations.literal: Shiru's seal method took the Two Li as patriarchs, expanding and contracting freely, deriving it from Shi Zhou, slightly mixing in clerical intent, cutting the tip to obtain forceful turns; the letterforms were slightly square, close to Qin and Han stele crowns.
translations.idiomatic: His seal script followed the Two Li masters, bold in expansion and contraction, rooted in Shi Zhou with a touch of clerical manner; he pared the tip for sharp turns, and his slightly square forms neared Qin–Han stele crowns.

sentences.zh: 分書結體嚴重，約嶧山、國山之法而為之。

translations.literal: His demotic script's structure was grave and weighty, fashioned by condensing the methods of Mount Yi and Mount Guo.
translations.idiomatic: His clerical structures were grave and weighty, distilled from the manners of the Yi Mountain and Guoshan steles.

sentences.zh: 自謂：「吾篆未及陽冰，而分不減梁鵠。

translations.literal: He said of himself: "My seal has not reached Yang Bing, but my demotic is no less than Liang Hu."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "My seal script has not matched Li Yangbing, but my clerical is no worse than Liang Hu's."

sentences.zh: 客梅氏八年，學既成，遍遊名山水，以書刻自給。

translations.literal: He was a guest of the Mei family for eight years; when his study was complete he traveled famous mountains and waters, supporting himself by writing and carving.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years with the Mei clan completed his training; he then toured famous landscapes, living by calligraphy and carving.

sentences.zh: 遊黃山，至歙，鬻篆於賈肆。

translations.literal: Traveling to Mount Huang he reached She and sold seal script in shops.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Huang and in She he sold seal script in market stalls.

sentences.zh: 編修張惠言故深究秦篆，時館修撰金榜家，偶見石如書，語榜曰：「今日得見上蔡真跡。

translations.literal: Compiler Zhang Huiyan had long studied Qin seal script deeply; he was then staying at Compiler Jin Bang's home, chanced upon Shiru's writing, and said to Bang: "Today I have seen the true traces of Shang Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Zhang Huiyan, a deep student of Qin seal script, was lodging with compiler Jin Bang when he chanced on Shiru's work and told Bang, "Today I have seen the authentic hand of Cai Yong of Shang.

sentences.zh: 」乃冒雨同訪於荒寺，榜備禮客之於家。

translations.literal: " Then in the rain they visited him together at a deserted temple; Bang prepared full rites and received him as a guest at home.
translations.idiomatic: " They braved rain to find him in a ruined temple; Bang then entertained him at home with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 薦於尚書曹文埴，偕至京師，大學士劉墉、副都御史陸錫熊皆驚異曰：「千數百年無此作矣！

translations.literal: He was recommended to Minister Cao Wenyan and went with him to the capital; Grand Secretary Liu Yong and Vice Censor-in-chief Lu Xixiong were all startled and said: "For a thousand and several hundred years there has been no work like this!
translations.idiomatic: Recommended to Minister Cao Wenyan, he went to the capital. Grand Secretary Liu Yong and Vice Censor Lu Xixiong marveled: "Nothing like this in a thousand years!

sentences.zh: 」時京師論篆、分者，多宗內閣學士翁方綱，方綱以石如不至其門，力詆之。

translations.literal: " At that time those in the capital who discussed seal and demotic script mostly followed Grand Secretary Weng Fanggang; Fanggang, because Shiru did not come to his door, denounced him forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: " In the capital, seal and clerical circles mostly followed Weng Fanggang, who attacked Shiru bitterly because he never paid court.

sentences.zh: 石如乃去，客兩湖總督畢沅，沅故好客，吳中名士多集節署，裘馬都麗，石如獨布衣徒步。

translations.literal: Shiru then departed and became a guest of the Huguang Governor-General Bi Yuan; Yuan had always loved guests, and many famous scholars of Wu gathered at his headquarters in fur coats and splendid horses, while Shiru alone wore plain cloth and walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru left for Governor-General Bi Yuan of Huguang, whose salon drew Wu literati in splendid dress while Shiru alone came in plain cloth on foot.

sentences.zh: 居三年，辭歸，沅為置田宅，俾終老。

translations.literal: After three years he took leave to return; Yuan set up fields and a house for him so that he might end his days in peace.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he retired; Yuan gave him land and a house for his old age.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，觴之，曰：「山人，吾幕府一服清涼散也！

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Yuan toasted him and said: "Mountain man, you are my headquarters' dose of cooling powder!
translations.idiomatic: As he left, Yuan raised a cup and said, "Hermit, you are the cooling powder for my staff!

sentences.zh: 」石如年四十六始娶，常往來江、淮間，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: " Shiru married only at forty-six, often traveled between the Yangtze and Huai, and died at sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: " He married at forty-six, traveled between the Yangtze and Huai, and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 子傳密，初名廷璽，字守之。

translations.literal: His son Chuanmi, original name Tingxi, styled Shouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuanmi, born Tingxi and styled Shouzhi,

sentences.zh: 從李兆洛學，晚客曾國籓幕。

translations.literal: studied under Li Zhaoluo and in later years was a client in Zeng Guofan's staff.
translations.idiomatic: studied under Li Zhaoluo and later served in Zeng Guofan's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 能以篆書世其家。

translations.literal: He was able to carry on the family through seal script.
translations.idiomatic: He carried on the family name through seal script.

sentences.zh: 當乾、嘉之間，嘉定錢坫、陽湖錢伯坰，皆以書名。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns, Qian Dian of Jiading and Qian Boxun of Yanghu were both renowned for calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong–Jiaqing era, Qian Dian of Jiading and Qian Boxun of Yanghu were both famed for writing.

sentences.zh: 坫自負其篆直接陽冰，嘗遊焦山，見壁間篆書心經，嘆為陽冰之亞。

translations.literal: Dian prided himself that his seal script directly followed Yang Bing; once traveling to Mount Jiao he saw the Heart Sutra in seal script on a wall and sighed that it was next to Yang Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Dian boasted that his seal script followed Li Yangbing directly. At Mount Jiao he saw a wall Heart Sutra in seal script and took it for Yangbing's equal.

sentences.zh: 既而知為石如所作，摭其不合六書者以為詆。

translations.literal: When he learned it was Shiru's work he gathered instances not conforming to the Six Scripts and used them for slander.
translations.idiomatic: Learning it was Shiru's, he collected alleged violations of the Six Scripts to attack him.

sentences.zh: 伯坰故服石如篆、分為絕業，及見其行、草，歎曰：「此楊少師神境也！

translations.literal: Boxun had long admired Shiru's seal and demotic as supreme craft; when he saw his running and cursive script he sighed: "This is the divine realm of Yang Shaoshi!
translations.idiomatic: Boxun had revered Shiru's seal and clerical as supreme; seeing his running and cursive, he cried, "This is the spirit-realm of Yang Ningshi!

sentences.zh: 」復與論筆法不合，遂助坫詆之尤力。

translations.literal: " But when they again discussed brush methods and disagreed, he then helped Dian slander him with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet when they debated brush method and clashed, he joined Dian's attacks with special zeal.

sentences.zh: 坫見儒林傳。

translations.literal: Dian appears in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Dian has a biography in the Confucian Scholars section.

sentences.zh: 伯坰，字魯斯，自號僕射山人，尚書維城從子。

translations.literal: Boxun, styled Lusi, called himself the Mountain Man of the Vice Director and was a nephew of Minister Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Boxun, styled Lusi and calling himself the Vice-Director Hermit, was a nephew of Minister Qian Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 少孤，力學，工詩嗜酒，廣交遊，以國子監生終。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied strenuously, was skilled in poetry and fond of wine, made wide friendships, and ended as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he studied hard, wrote poetry, loved wine, cultivated many friends, and ended his days as an Imperial Academy student.

sentences.zh: 書學顏平原、李北海，嘗曰：「古人用兔毫，故書有中線，今用羊毫，其精者乃成雙鉤。

translations.literal: In calligraphy he studied Yan Pingyuan and Li Beihai, and once said: "The ancients used rabbit hair, so writing had a center line; today we use goat hair, and only the finest achieve the double hook.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Yan Zhenqing and Li Yong and said, "Ancients used rabbit hair, so strokes had a center line; with goat hair today only the finest achieve the double hook.

sentences.zh: 吾躭此五十年，才十得三四。

translations.literal: I have devoted myself to this fifty years and have attained only three or four parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: I have pursued this fifty years and mastered barely three parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 」論者謂自劉墉歿，正、行書以伯坰為第一。

translations.literal: " Critics said that since Liu Yong's death, in regular and running script Boxun was first.
translations.idiomatic: " Critics ranked him first in regular and running script after Liu Yong's death.

sentences.zh: 其執筆，虛小指，以三指包管外，與大指相拒，側毫入紙，助怒張之勢。

translations.literal: In holding the brush he left the little finger idle, wrapped the shaft outside with three fingers opposing the thumb, and sent the side hairs into the paper to assist the momentum of angry expansion.
translations.idiomatic: He held the brush with the little finger free, three fingers wrapping the shaft against the thumb, driving the side hairs into the paper for explosive force.

sentences.zh: 指腕皆不動，以肘來去，斥古今相承撥鐙之說。

translations.literal: Fingers and wrist did not move; he used the elbow coming and going, and rejected the stirrup-pressing doctrine handed down from ancient to modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Fingers and wrist stayed still; the elbow moved the stroke. He rejected the inherited stirrup-pressing doctrine.

sentences.zh: 石如作書，則懸腕雙鉤，管隨指轉，兩家法大殊。

translations.literal: When Shiru wrote, he suspended the wrist with double hook and the shaft followed the fingers' turn—the methods of the two houses were greatly different.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru wrote with suspended wrist and double hook, the shaft turning with the fingers—the two schools could hardly differ more.

sentences.zh: 吳育，字山子，江蘇吳江人。

translations.literal: Wu Yu, styled Shanzhi, was a native of Wujiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu, styled Shanzhi, came from Wujiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 與包世臣、李兆洛遊，能文，工書。

translations.literal: He associated with Bao Shichen and Li Zhaoluo, was able in literary composition, and skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: A companion of Bao Shichen and Li Zhaoluo, he wrote well and practiced calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 謂：「下筆須使筆毫平鋪紙上，乃四面圓足，此陽冰篆法，書家真秘密語。

translations.literal: He said: "When putting the brush down one must make the hairs lie flat on the paper, then on all four sides they are round and full—this is Yang Bing's seal method, the calligrapher's true secret words.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Lay the brush hairs flat on the paper so the stroke rounds on every side—that is Yangbing's seal secret, the calligrapher's true whisper.

sentences.zh: 」世臣取其說。

translations.literal: " Shichen adopted his doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao Shichen adopted this teaching.

sentences.zh: 育篆書尤工，法與石如差近。

translations.literal: Yu was especially accomplished in seal script; his method differed little from Shiru's.
translations.idiomatic: Yu excelled in seal script in a manner close to Shiru's.

sentences.zh: 楊沂孫，字詠春，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Yang Yisun, styled Yongchun, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yisun, styled Yongchun, came from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十三年舉人，官安徽鳳陽知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate and served as prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He took the provincial degree in Daoguang 23 and served as prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，遂不出，自號濠叟，少學於李兆洛，治週、秦諸子。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he returned and would not emerge, styled himself the Old Man of the Moat, studied in youth under Li Zhaoluo, and worked on the masters of Zhou and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he retired for good, calling himself the Old Man of the Moat. He had studied under Li Zhaoluo in youth and worked on Zhou and Qin philosophers.

sentences.zh: 耽書法，尤致力於篆、籀，著文字解說問譌，欲補苴段玉裁、王筠所未備。

translations.literal: He was devoted to calligraphy and especially applied himself to seal and large-seal scripts, authoring Explanatory Questions and Corrections on Characters, intending to supplement what Duan Yucai and Wang Yun had not provided.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to calligraphy, he focused on seal and large-seal script and wrote Explanatory Questions on Characters to fill gaps left by Duan Yucai and Wang Yun.

sentences.zh: 又考上古逮史籀、李斯，折衷於許慎，作在昔篇。

translations.literal: He also examined antiquity down through Shi Zhou and Li Si, reconciling them with Xu Shen, and composed the In Times Past.
translations.idiomatic: He traced writing from antiquity through Shi Zhou and Li Si, reconciled them with Xu Shen, and wrote In Times Past.

sentences.zh: 篆、隸宗石如，而多自得。

translations.literal: In seal and clerical script he took Shiru as patriarch yet had much of his own attainment.
translations.idiomatic: His seal and clerical work followed Shiru yet owed much to his own insight.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾書篆、籀，頡頏鄧氏，得意處或過之；

translations.literal: He once said: "In my seal and large-seal script I rival the Deng clan; in inspired passages I sometimes surpass them;
translations.idiomatic: He said, "In seal and large-seal I rival the Deng school and sometimes surpass it where inspiration strikes;

sentences.zh: 分、隸則不能及也。

translations.literal: in demotic and clerical script I cannot reach them."
translations.idiomatic: but in demotic and clerical I cannot match them."

sentences.zh: 」光緒七年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Guangxu he died at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in Guangxu 7 at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 沂孫同時工篆、籀者，又推吳大澂，自有傳。

translations.literal: Among those of Yisun's time skilled in seal and large-seal script, Wu Dacheng was also esteemed and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Among contemporaries in seal script, Wu Dacheng was also celebrated and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 吳熙載，初名廷颺，以字行，後又字讓之，江蘇儀徵人。

translations.literal: Wu Xizai, original name Tingyang, went by his style name and later also styled Rangzhi, was a native of Yizheng in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xizai, born Tingyang and known by his style (later Rangzhi), came from Yizheng in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 先世居江寧，父明煌，始遊揚州，善相人術。

translations.literal: His forebears dwelt in Jiangning; his father Minghuang first traveled to Yangzhou and was skilled in physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in Nanjing; his father Minghuang moved to Yangzhou and practiced physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 熙載為諸生，博學多能，從包世臣學書。

translations.literal: Xizai was a licentiate, broadly learned and multi-talented, and studied calligraphy under Bao Shichen.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate of wide learning, he studied calligraphy under Bao Shichen.

sentences.zh: 世臣創明北朝書派，溯源窮流，為一家之學。

translations.literal: Shichen elucidated the Northern Dynasties calligraphic school, tracing sources and exhausting currents, forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen defined the Northern Dynasties school of calligraphy, tracing its sources into a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 其筆法兼採同時黃乙生、王良士、吳育、硃昂之、鄧石如諸人之說。

translations.literal: His brush methods combined the doctrines of his contemporaries Huang Yisheng, Wang Liangshi, Wu Yu, Zhu Angzhi, Deng Shiru, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His brush theory drew on Huang Yisheng, Wang Liangshi, Wu Yu, Zhu Angzhi, Deng Shiru, and others of his day.

sentences.zh: 執筆，食指高鉤，大指加食指、中指之間，中指內鉤，小指貼名指外拒，管向左迤，後稍偃，若指鼻準。

translations.literal: In holding the brush the forefinger hooks high, the thumb is placed between forefinger and middle finger, the middle finger hooks inward, the little finger presses the ring finger outward in resistance, the shaft bends leftward and later leans slightly as if pointing at the nose.
translations.idiomatic: He held the brush with a high forefinger hook, thumb between fore and middle fingers, middle finger hooked inward, little finger bracing the ring finger, shaft angling left then tilting as if toward the nose.

sentences.zh: 運鋒，使筆毫平鋪紙上，筆筆斷而後起。

translations.literal: In moving the tip he made the hairs lie flat on the paper; each stroke broke off and then rose again.
translations.idiomatic: Moving the tip, he laid the hairs flat; each stroke lifted before the next began.

sentences.zh: 結字計白當黑，使左右牝牡相得，自謂合古人八法、九宮之旨。

translations.literal: In structuring characters he calculated white against black, making left and right male and female harmonize, and claimed to accord with the ancients' Eight Methods and Nine Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He balanced white space against black and paired left and right like yin and yang, claiming this matched the ancients' Eight Methods and Nine Palaces.

sentences.zh: 熙載恪守師法，世臣真、行、藁草無不工，嗜篆、分而未致力，熙載篆、分功力尤深。

translations.literal: Xizai strictly kept his master's methods; Shichen was accomplished in regular, running, and draft cursive but loved seal and demotic without applying effort—Xizai's power in seal and demotic was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai kept his master's teaching faithfully. Shichen excelled in regular, running, and draft cursive but neglected seal and clerical; Xizai's depth lay precisely there.

sentences.zh: 复縱筆作畫，亦有士氣。

translations.literal: He also freely wielded the brush in painting, which likewise had scholarly air.
translations.idiomatic: He painted as well, with a literati air.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xianfeng reign.

sentences.zh: 與熙載同受包氏法者，江都梅植之蘊生，甘泉楊亮季子，高涼黃洵修存，餘姚毛長齡仰蘇，旌德姚配中仲虞，松桃楊承汪挹之。

translations.literal: Those who like Xizai received the Bao school's methods included Mei Zhizhi Yunsheng of Jiangdu, Yang Liang Jizi of Ganquan, Huang Xunxiu Cun of Gaoliang, Mao Changling Yangsu of Yuyao, Yao Peizhong Zhongyu of Jingde, and Yang Cheng Wang Yizhi of Songtao.
translations.idiomatic: Others of Bao's school included Mei Zhizhi of Jiangdu, Yang Liang of Ganquan, Huang Xunxiu of Gaoliang, Mao Changling of Yuyao, Yao Peizhong of Jingde, and Yang Cheng of Songtao.

sentences.zh: 配中詳儒林傳。

translations.literal: Peizhong is treated in detail in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Peizhong is treated at length in the Confucian Scholars biographies.

sentences.zh: 植之，道光十九年舉人。

translations.literal: Zhizhi became a provincial graduate in the nineteenth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi passed the provincial examination in Daoguang 19.

sentences.zh: 通經，以詩鳴，世臣尤稱其書。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics, was renowned for poetry, and Shichen especially praised his calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: A classicist famed for poetry, he won Shichen's highest praise for calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 謂其跌宕遒麗，段煉舊搨，血脈精氣，奔赴腕下，熙載未之敢先。

translations.literal: He said it was free and bold, forceful and beautiful, tempering old rubbings section by section, with blood, pulse, essence, and spirit rushing to the wrist—Xizai did not dare go before him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen called it bold and beautiful, old rubbings refined stroke by stroke, spirit pouring to the wrist—Xizai did not dare rank above him.

sentences.zh: 又得琴法於吳思伯之女弟子顏夫人，獨具神解。

translations.literal: He also obtained qin method from Lady Yan, a female disciple of Wu Sibo's daughter, and possessed a unique spiritual understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He learned the qin from Lady Yan, disciple of Wu Sibo's daughter, with rare intuitive mastery.

sentences.zh: 糾正思伯傳譜，於古操製曲之故，輒能知之。

translations.literal: He corrected Sibo's transmitted tablature and generally knew the reasons behind ancient pieces and how melodies were composed.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected Sibo's transmitted scores and understood why ancient pieces were composed as they were.

sentences.zh: 自署所居曰嵇庵。

translations.literal: He styled his dwelling the Ji Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: He named his studio the Ji Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 配中與有同嗜，著琴學二卷。

translations.literal: Peizhong shared the same passion and authored two fascicles on Qin Studies.
translations.idiomatic: Peizhong shared his passion and wrote two fascicles on Qin Studies.

sentences.zh: 植之五十而卒，琴法未有傳書。

translations.literal: Zhizhi died at fifty; his qin method was not transmitted in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi died at fifty without leaving his qin teaching in writing.

sentences.zh: 亮，世為將家，襲騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Liang came from a hereditary military family and inherited the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Liang came from a military line and inherited the hereditary post of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 篤學敦行，江、淮間士大夫多稱之。

translations.literal: Sincere in study and solid in conduct, he was much praised by scholar-officials between the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in learning and upright in conduct, he was widely praised among Jiang-Huai literati.

sentences.zh: 書亞於熙載。

translations.literal: His calligraphy was second only to Xizai's.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy he ranked just below Xizai.

sentences.zh: 合肥沈用熙最後出，至光緒末始卒，年近八十。

translations.literal: Shen Yongxi of Hefei appeared last; he did not die until near the end of Guangxu, nearly eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yongxi of Hefei was the last of the line; he lived nearly to eighty and died near the end of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 畢生守師法，最為包門老弟子。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he kept his master's methods and was the oldest disciple of the Bao school.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Bao's methods all his life and was the school's senior surviving disciple.

sentences.zh: 世臣敘次清一代書人為五品，分九等：「平和簡靜，遒麗天成，曰神品；

translations.literal: Shichen arranged Qing calligraphers in five grades divided into nine ranks: "Even, peaceful, simple, and still; forceful, beautiful, and heaven-born—this is the divine grade;
translations.idiomatic: Shichen ranked Qing calligraphers in five grades and nine ranks: "Even, calm, simple, and still; vigorous, beautiful, and natural—this is the divine grade;

sentences.zh: 醖釀無跡，橫直相安，曰妙品；

translations.literal: brewed without trace, horizontal and vertical at peace—this is the subtle grade;
translations.idiomatic: effortless brewing, horizontal and vertical at ease—this is the subtle grade;

sentences.zh: 逐跡尋源，思力交至，曰能品；

translations.literal: pursuing traces and seeking sources, thought and force both arriving—this is the able grade;
translations.idiomatic: tracing forms and seeking sources, mind and force meeting—this is the able grade;

sentences.zh: 楚調自歌，不謬風雅，曰逸品；

translations.literal: Chu tune self-sung, not deviating from elegance—this is the transcendent grade;
translations.idiomatic: singing in one's own Chu mode without betraying the Odes—this is the transcendent grade;

sentences.zh: 墨守跡象，雅有門庭，曰佳品。

translations.literal: ink guarding traces and forms, elegantly having a school gate—this is the fine grade.
translations.idiomatic: faithful to received forms yet with a school of one's own—this is the fine grade.

sentences.zh: 神品一人，鄧石如隸及篆書。

translations.literal: Divine grade, one person: Deng Shiru's clerical and seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Divine grade (one): Deng Shiru in clerical and seal script.

sentences.zh: 妙品上一人，鄧石如分及真書；

translations.literal: Subtle grade upper, one person: Deng Shiru's demotic and regular script;
translations.idiomatic: Upper subtle grade (one): Deng Shiru in demotic and regular script;

sentences.zh: 妙品下二人，劉墉小真書，姚鼐行草書。

translations.literal: Subtle grade lower, two people: Liu Yong's small regular script, Yao Nai's running-cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: Lower subtle grade (two): Liu Yong in small regular script, Yao Nai in running-cursive.

sentences.zh: 能品上七人，釋邱山真及行書，宋玨分榜書，傅山草書，姜宸英行書，鄧石如草書，劉墉榜書，黃乙生行榜書；

translations.literal: Able grade upper, seven people: Monk Qiushan's regular and running script, Song Jue's demotic plaque script, Fu Shan's cursive script, Jiang Chenying's running script, Deng Shiru's cursive script, Liu Yong's plaque script, Huang Yisheng's running plaque script;
translations.idiomatic: Upper able grade (seven): Monk Qiushan in regular and running script; Song Jue in demotic plaque script; Fu Shan in cursive; Jiang Chenying in running script; Deng Shiru in cursive; Liu Yong in plaque script; Huang Yisheng in running plaque script;

sentences.zh: 能品下二十三人，王鐸草書，周亮工草書，笪重光行書，吳大來草書，趙潤草榜書，張照行書，劉紹庭草榜書，吳襄行書，翟賜履草書，王澍行書，週於禮行書，梁巘真及行書，翁方綱行書，於令行書，巴慰祖分書，顧光旭行書，張惠言篆書，王文治方寸真書，劉墉行書，汪庭桂分書，錢伯坰行及榜書，陳希祖行書，黃乙生小真行書。

translations.literal: Able grade lower, twenty-three people: Wang Duo's cursive script, Zhou Lianggong's cursive script, Da Chongguang's running script, Wu Dalai's cursive script, Zhao Run's cursive plaque script, Zhang Zhao's running script, Liu Shaoting's cursive plaque script, Wu Xiang's running script, Zhai Cilü's cursive script, Wang Shu's running script, Zhou Yuli's running script, Liang Yan's regular and running script, Weng Fanggang's running script, Yu Ling's running script, Ba Weizu's demotic script, Gu Guangxu's running script, Zhang Huiyan's seal script, Wang Wenzhi's square-inch regular script, Liu Yong's running script, Wang Tinggui's demotic script, Qian Boxun's running and plaque script, Chen Xizu's running script, Huang Yisheng's small regular-running script.
translations.idiomatic: Lower able grade (twenty-three): Wang Duo, Zhou Lianggong, Da Chongguang, Wu Dalai, Zhao Run, Zhang Zhao, Liu Shaoting, Wu Xiang, Zhai Cilü, Wang Shu, Zhou Yuli, Liang Yan, Weng Fanggang, Yu Ling, Ba Weizu, Gu Guangxu, Zhang Huiyan, Wang Wenzhi, Liu Yong, Wang Tinggui, Qian Boxun, Chen Xizu, and Huang Yisheng—in the scripts named above.

sentences.zh: 逸品上十五人，顧炎武正書，蕭雲從行書，釋雪浪行書，鄭簠分及行書，高其佩行書，陳洪綬行書，程邃行書，紀映鍾行書，金農分書，張鵬翀行書，袁枚行書，硃筠藁書，硃珪真書，鄧石如行書，宋鎔行書；

translations.literal: Transcendent grade upper, fifteen people: Gu Yanwu's standard script, Xiao Yuncong's running script, Monk Xuelang's running script, Zheng Fu's demotic and running script, Gao Qipei's running script, Chen Hongshou's running script, Cheng Sui's running script, Ji Yingzhong's running script, Jin Nong's demotic script, Zhang Pengchong's running script, Yuan Mei's running script, Zhu Yun's draft script, Zhu Gui's regular script, Deng Shiru's running script, Song Rong's running script;
translations.idiomatic: Upper transcendent grade (fifteen): Gu Yanwu, Xiao Yuncong, Monk Xuelang, Zheng Fu, Gao Qipei, Chen Hongshou, Cheng Sui, Ji Yingzhong, Jin Nong, Zhang Pengchong, Yuan Mei, Zhu Yun, Zhu Gui, Deng Shiru, and Song Rong—in the scripts listed.

sentences.zh: 逸品下十六人，王時敏行及分書，硃彝尊分及行書，程京萼行書，釋道濟行書，趙青藜真及行書，錢載行書，程瑤田小真書，巴慰祖行書，汪中行書，畢涵行書，陳淮行書，姚鼐小真書，程世淳行書，李天澂行書，伊秉綬行書，張桂岩行書。

sentences.zh: 」九品共九十七人，重見者六人，實九十一人。

translations.literal: " The nine grades totaled ninety-seven persons; six appeared twice, so in fact ninety-one persons.
translations.idiomatic: " The nine ranks list ninety-seven entries; six names repeat, so ninety-one individuals in all.

sentences.zh: 復增能品上一人，張琦真、行及分書；

translations.literal: He further added to able grade upper one person: Zhang Qi's regular, running, and demotic script;
translations.idiomatic: He later added one to the upper able grade: Zhang Qi in regular, running, and demotic script;

sentences.zh: 能品下三人，於書佃行書，段玉立小真及草書，吳德旋行書。

translations.literal: able grade lower three people: Yu Shudian's running script, Duan Yuli's small regular and cursive script, Wu Dexuan's running script.
translations.idiomatic: lower able grade (three): Yu Shudian in running script; Duan Yuli in small regular and cursive; Wu Dexuan in running script.

sentences.zh: 佳品上六人，吳育篆及行書，方履籛分書，梅植之行書，硃昂之行書，李兆洛行書，徐準宜真書。

translations.idiomatic: Upper fine grade (six): Wu Yu in seal and running script; Fang Lüqian in demotic; Mei Zhizhi, Zhu Angzhi, and Li Zhaoluo in running script; Xu Zhunyi in regular script.

sentences.zh: 其後包氏之學盛行，咸、同以來，以書名者，何紹基、張裕釗、翁同龢三家最著，並見他傳。

translations.literal: Afterward the Bao school's learning flourished; from the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns onward, those renowned for calligraphy were most famous in the three houses of He Shaoji, Zhang Yuzhao, and Weng Tonghe—all appear in other biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bao's school prevailed. From the Xianfeng and Tongzhi eras, He Shaoji, Zhang Yuzhao, and Weng Tonghe were the most celebrated calligraphers—all treated in other chapters.

sentences.zh: 紹基宗顏平原法，晚復出入漢分；

translations.literal: Shaoji took Yan Pingyuan's method as patriarch and in later years again moved in and out of Han demotic script;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoji followed Yan Zhenqing and in later years moved freely between Han clerical manners;

sentences.zh: 裕釗源出於包氏；

translations.literal: Yuzhao's source came from the Bao clan;
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhao descended from Bao's line;

sentences.zh: 同龢規模閎變，不為諸家所囿，為一代後勁雲。

translations.literal: Tonghe's scope was broad and transforming, not confined by the various schools, and he was the sustaining force of a generation, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe worked on a grand, changing scale, unbound by any single school, and stood as the late vigor of the age.
